prompt.context: We have just been approached by the council of Dracula, an isolated city of 900,000 people. The council is considering whether to approve the request to allow a steel supplier to open a factory next to an important dam on the outskirts of the city.
prompt.question: What advice do we have for the council?

clarifying_info.a: It is used to generate hydroelectricity for the city.

clarifying_info.q: Are there other energy sources for the city?
How long will the construction of the factory take?
On what basis should this decision be made?
What is the city population growth rate?
Why does the plant need to be built next to the dam?
clarifying_info.a: It needs to use the water for its manufacturing process.

clarifying_info.q: Are there other locations the plant is considering?

exhibits.title: Dam Water Level Changes Over a Year
exhibits.shows: A chart of dam water level (meters) across Q1–Q4, with a note that hydroelectricity generation occurs at the end of each quarter. Accompanied by a table listing four sources (Rain, Evaporation, Hydroelectricity generation, Water for residents) with water level change in meters per month and meters per year.

table.note: occurs at end of each quarter

exhibits.title: Energy Generation From Dam
exhibits.shows: A lookup table mapping dam water level ranges (meters) to electricity generation (MWh).

framework: 1. The steel factory: (a) Construction issues — pollution, protests, unions; (b) Jobs for residents during construction and operation; (c) Tax revenue for the city; (d) Cost and time to build

2. The city of Dracula: (a) Current uses of the dam — recreational, hydroelectricity generation, water resource for residents; (b) Demographics of residents; (c) Primary industries; (d) Population growth
Key steer: While environmental concerns are natural, the interviewer should guide toward the dam's role in hydroelectricity generation and the impact of reduced water levels on power supply.

questions.prompt: What are some of the major inflows and outflows into and out of the dam?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify: Inflows — Rain, water from wastewater treatment plants, runoff from nearby lakes/mountains. Outflows — Evaporation, hydroelectricity generation, water for residents' homes, water for factories in the city.

questions.prompt: Based on Exhibit 1, what are the inflows and outflows from the dam per quarter?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify: (1) At the start of each quarter the water level is 85 m. (2) During the quarter, due to rain, evaporation, and resident water usage, the level increases by 21 m to 96 m. (3) At the end of the quarter, hydroelectricity generation causes the level to fall by 21 m, restarting the cycle. Rain is the only inflow; all other sources are outflows.

math.setup: Convert annual/monthly rates to quarterly rates. Quarter = 3 months.
steps: Hydroelectricity generation: 48 m/year ÷ 4 = 12 m/quarter (outflow, end of quarter)

Net during quarter (before hydro): +21 m rain − 3.75 m evap − 5.25 m residents = +12 m... but exhibit shows level rises from 85 to 96, i.e. +11 m. Guidance: rain is the sole inflow; evaporation and resident water offset to give a net +11 m rise to 96 m, then hydro generation drops it 12 m back toward 85 m, completing the cycle.
math.answer: Inflow: 21 m/quarter (rain). Outflows: 3.75 m evaporation + 5.25 m residents + 12 m hydroelectricity = 21 m/quarter. Net = 0, cycle restarts each quarter at 85 m rising to 96 m then back.

questions.prompt: How much power does the dam generate per quarter, and is this sustainable for the city? (Use Exhibit 2. Note: the steel factory will reduce the water level by an additional 3 meters per quarter.)
questions.guidance: Candidate should: (1) Read from Exhibit 2 that 96 m water level → 2,400,000 MWh/quarter. (2) Calculate city demand: 900,000 residents x 2 MWh/quarter = 1,800,000 MWh/quarter — currently sustainable. (3) Recognize that the steel factory adds 3 m/quarter of outflow, making total outflow 24 m/quarter vs. 21 m/quarter inflow, a net loss of 3 m/quarter. (4) Track the declining water level quarter by quarter until it drops below 70 m, at which point generation falls to 1,800,000 MWh = exactly demand, and below 70 m it becomes insufficient. This happens after 9 quarters (2.25 years).

math.setup: Starting water level at end of quarter (after hydro generation): 96 m. Each quarter the level drops by 3 m net (factory outflow exceeds inflow). Check against 70 m threshold where generation = 1,800,000 MWh = city demand.
steps: Q9: 72 − 3 = 69 m → 1,500,000 MWh (BELOW demand of 1,800,000 MWh)
math.answer: After 9 quarters (2.25 years), the water level drops below 70 m and the dam can no longer generate enough electricity for the city's 900,000 residents. This assumes no population growth.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the major inflows and outflows into and out of the dam?

categories.name: Inflows
ideas: Runoff from nearby lakes or mountains

categories.name: Outflows
ideas: Water for factories in the city

recommendation: We would recommend against the construction of the steel factory in its current form.
risks: Significant pushback from residents who view the factory as a source of employment (unemployment rate is 15%)
The steel factory could generate significant tax revenue for Dracula
Rejection may signal to other companies that doing business in Dracula is difficult
next_steps: Explore alternative sources of energy generation so the city is not solely reliant on the dam for electricity
Discuss with the steel factory whether it can identify an alternative water source for its production process
Investigate whether water can be pumped into the dam from a neighboring city to offset the factory's usage
